item.title: ECB Keeps Rate Steady to Gauge Iran War Impact on Inflation
item.description: The European Central Bank kept borrowing costs unchanged, awaiting data to judge whether price pressures unleashed by the Iran war require additional tightening.

item.title: South Africa Fund Plans $609 Million VC Raise With Exits Rising
item.description: A key South Africa fund plans to raise as much as 10 billion rand ($609 million) in venture capital to help scale high-growth startups, a move that would expand its technology sector and accelerate the development of one the continent’s most mature startup markets.

item.title: US Stock Futures Drop as Traders Focus on AI Spending, Oil Jumps
item.description: US stock futures retreated as worries over artificial-intelligence spending weighed on sentiment while oil prices closed in on $100 a barrel. Traders braced for more key earnings from Intel Corp., due later in the afternoon.

item.title: Cellnex Studies Strategic Options After Share Price Slump
item.description: Cellnex Telecom SA is evaluating strategic options, according to people familiar with the matter, as the wireless tower operator looks at ways to grapple with its debt load and weak share price.

item.title: GCM Grosvenor Raises $1.2 Billion for Credit Secondaries Push
item.description: GCM Grosvenor has raised $1.2 billion for its first dedicated fund strategy targeting credit secondaries.

item.title: Alphabet’s Century Bond Has Now Lost a 10th of Its Face Value
item.description: A 100-year bond that Alphabet Inc. issued earlier this year in the sterling market as it gorged on debt around the world has dropped below 90 pence on the pound for the first time.

item.title: Google Says it Holds $94 Billion in SpaceX Shares After IPO
item.description: Alphabet Inc.’s Google said its equity holdings include $94.1 billion in SpaceX shares, after the space-and-AI company’s blockbuster initial public offering.

item.title: India May Allow Portfolio Managers to Take Unhedged Short Bets
item.description: India’s securities regulator has proposed allowing domestic portfolio management service providers to take short positions in equity derivatives for the first time, easing rules for professional money managers even as it tightens oversight of retail trading.

item.title: JPMorgan Quants Say Strongest Earnings Upgrades Are in Europe
item.description: Europe now leads the world as the region with the sharpest upgrades to corporate earnings estimates from analysts, according to JPMorgan Chase & Co.

item.title: Kuehne+Nagel Weighs Options For Apex Logistics Unit
item.description: Kuehne+Nagel International AG is considering strategic options for its Apex Logistics unit, an Asia-focused freight forwarder, people with knowledge of the matter said.

item.title: Infosys Cuts Revenue Forecast on Muted IT Services Demand
item.description: Infosys Ltd. cut the upper end of its sales growth outlook as global clients slow down technology spending at a time of elevated interest rates and geopolitical conflicts.

item.title: Global Reliance on US Equities Flashes Alarm, Along With China Corporate Debt
item.description: US stocks are stretched on historical valuation metrics, posing an economic risk if sentiment turns.

item.title: Keeping Kids Safe Online From AI Shows US and China on Different Paths
item.description: China’s proactive approach to regulating AI and social media appears to be working

item.title: Turkey Holds Rates as Oil Price Spike Tests Inflation Fight
item.description: Turkey’s central bank left interest rates unchanged on Thursday, with the war in the Middle East and rising energy prices threatening to derail a fragile disinflation process.

item.title: Houthi attacks on shipping in the Red Sea
item.description: Container lines have been sailing south of Africa since late 2023 to avoid Houthi attacks

item.title: Tinder Brings In-Person Dating Events to More Cities in the US, Europe
item.description: Tinder is expanding its in-person singles events to new markets across the US and Europe following a successful test in Los Angeles that launched in March.

item.title: Dangote Reverts to Pricing Gasoline in Naira After Dollar Switch
item.description: Dangote Petroleum Refinery & Petrochemicals Fze reverted to the sale of petroleum products in naira, a week after switching to sales in US dollars.

item.title: AI Debt Competing with Treasuries Is Adding to Lofty US Yields
item.description: The US 30-year bond yield has held above 5% for the longest stretch since the start of the financial crisis.

item.title: AI, Climate Change Are Creating a Perfect Storm for US Power Grids
item.description: A perfect storm is brewing for more grid emergencies and service disruptions.

item.title: T-Mobile Revenue Misses Expectations as Subscriber Gains Slow
item.description: T-Mobile US Inc. reported revenue that missed analysts’ estimates amid modest gains in subscribers.

item.title: McCormick Will Add London Listing After Unilever Food Deal
item.description: McCormick & Co. has picked London as a secondary listing location, just months after striking a deal to combine with Unilever Plc’s food business and in a blow to Amsterdam’s hopes.

item.title: Pound Rally Fizzles as Burnham Keeps UK Fiscal Plans Unclear
item.description: The pound’s rally is at risk from the new UK government’s still unclear fiscal plans as well as the potential for fewer interest-rate hikes eroding the currency’s high-yield appeal.

item.title: Hedge Funds’ Favorite US Bond Trade Is Sputtering
item.description: Hedge funds’ most popular trade in the US bond market is showing signs of maxing out.

item.title: Google Fined €890 Million in EU Over Search, App Store Breaches
item.description: Alphabet Inc.’s Google was fined a total of €890 million ($1 billion) by the European Union for violating the bloc’s Digital Markets Act, in a decision that risks further inflaming tensions with US President Donald Trump.

item.title: Comcast Earnings Beat Estimates on Peacock, Box Office Successes
item.description: Comcast Corp. reported earnings that beat analysts’ estimates on key metrics, buoyed by the first-ever quarterly profitability at its Peacock streaming platform and a string of Hollywood hits.

item.title: Google Will Now Let Users Sign In to Accounts With a Selfie Video
item.description: Google is adding a selfie video option as a new way to sign in to accounts, providing an alternative for users who may be locked out due to a lost device or forgotten password.

item.title: Goldman Sachs, Absa See Ghana Rate Cuts Delayed by Iran War, Oil Prices
item.description: Goldman Sachs Group Inc. and Absa Group Ltd. believe the window for the Bank of Ghana to resume policy easing this year has closed due to fresh inflation pressures from renewed tensions in the Middle East

item.title: SpaceX Attempts Major Flight Test Again in Post-IPO Spotlight
item.description: SpaceX will again attempt a major test of its massive Starship rocket on Thursday after abandoning takeoff last week, exposing investors to the risks of the company’s rocky development cycle and heightening the stakes for the critical milestone.

item.title: Asian Oil Buyers in Talks With Saudis to Reroute Red Sea Flows
item.description: At least two Asian crude oil buyers are in talks with Saudi Aramco to potentially reroute flows around Africa after Houthi attacks on tankers in the Red Sea, according to traders familiar with the matter.
